answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil floods with per-identity stake and slashing: before its votes count, each agent locks a bond, a narrow ledge of capital it can lose. Every clone needs its own bond, so an attacker pays once per fake identity, and one dishonest vertex in a collusion ring triggers slashing that burns that deposit. Pseudonyms are as cheap as shale, yet shale makes poor collateral; without locked value the fake accounts carry no weight, so scaling the attack scales the bill.
